item.title: Beating Nerves
item.description: Speak clearly and confidently in front of any room, with practical techniques you can practise and a routine that makes you better every time. Lesson 1: Beating Nerves This lesson teaches you what nerves actually are and how to work with them, because nerves are where most speakers get stuck — and…

item.title: Structuring a Talk
item.description: Lesson 2: Structuring a Talk This lesson teaches you to structure a talk so listeners can follow it without effort. A good talk has one clear message, a beginning, a middle, and an ending that lands — and the listener should be able to repeat the message afterwards in one sentence. Structure is not…

item.title: Opening Strong
item.description: Lesson 3: Opening Strong This lesson teaches you to open strong, because the first minute of a talk decides whether the room listens or drifts. Listeners make a fast, mostly unconscious judgement in the opening moments: is this speaker worth my attention? That judgement is not about your talent —…

item.title: Voice and Body Language
item.description: Lesson 4: Voice and Body Language This lesson teaches you to use your voice and your body to support your words, because how you say something shapes how it is heard. A talk with strong content and a flat, rushed delivery loses the room; a talk with simple content and a clear, varied delivery holds…

item.title: Slides That Help Instead of Hurt
item.description: Lesson 5: Slides That Help Instead of Hurt This lesson teaches you to design slides that help the audience and never replace you as the speaker. Slides are a visual aid, not a script: their job is to show what words cannot show easily — a picture, a diagram, a short list — while you do the talking.…

item.title: Handling Questions
item.description: Lesson 6: Handling Questions This lesson teaches you to handle questions well, including hard ones, hostile ones, and ones you cannot answer. The question session is not an exam — it is the part of the talk where the audience gets to think with you, and it often determines what they remember. A…

item.title: Storytelling
item.description: Lesson 7: Storytelling This lesson teaches storytelling: how to tell short, honest stories that make your ideas stick in the listener's mind. Facts tell, but stories hold. An audience may forget your three points within a week, but they will remember the story of the morning the bins overflowed…

item.title: A Practice and Feedback Routine
item.description: Lesson 8: A Practice and Feedback Routine This final lesson builds your practice and feedback routine: a repeatable method for rehearsing any talk and getting better every time you give one.
